items.readable_text:
Content:
How do we calculate the area of a parallelogram, like the one below?

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/eac342d313b626c1fb529ec16a38e32d]

Content:
We can do this with the following formula:
[MATH: \textrm{Area} = \textrm{base} \times \textrm{height}]

Content:
Note that the height needs to be at a right angle to the base. This is very important.

Content:
Let's use this formula to determine the area of the parallelogram below.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/f61401f60b37be645cec927ff8be7c3f]

Content:
First, we write down the base and height of the parallelogram:
[MATH: base|= 8; height|= 4]

Content:
Substituting the values of the base and height into the formula, we get:
[MATH: Area|= base × height; = 8 × 4; = 32]

Content:
We'll show how to derive the formula at the end of the lesson.

items.title: Finding the Perimeter of a Parallelogram Given the Area

sections.normalized_html: What the perimeter of the parallelogram given that its area is [MATH: 48?]
sections.readable_text:
What the perimeter of the parallelogram given that its area is [MATH: 48?]

[IMG: /graphics/df4b29f34d3be81c318386eb5e2b0414]

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
Let's write down what we know:

[MATH: Area = 48; base =?; height = 4; side = 5]

The area of the parallelogram can be found by the following formula: [MATH: \textrm{Area} = \textrm{base} \times \textrm{height}]

Substituting the values of the area and height, we get [MATH: 48|= base × 4.]

Using the relationship between multiplication and division, we can solve for the base: [MATH: \textrm{base} = 48 \div 4 = 12]

Finally, the perimeter of the parallelogram is

[MATH: Perimeter|= (base + side) × 2; = (12 + 5) × 2; = 17 × 2; = 34.]
